The Gini index collapses the skewness of the bright-end luminosity function to a single statistic, and provides a measure for the light dominance of the BCG over other cluster members that is more robust than the magnitude gap. We argue that the Gini index is far less sensitive to short-term changes in the cluster dynamical state than the magnitude gap and solves its known degeneracies by taking the entire cluster membership into account, making G a more sensitive metric to long-term BCG assembly. We apply the magnitude gap and Gini index to a progenitor-selected sample of 92 South Pole Telescope- and Planck-selected cluster cores at 0 < z < 1 with corresponding Hubble Space Telescope F110W and F200LP and Sloan Digital Sky Survey g and r photometry. Based on both parametric and empirical tests, we find no statistical evidence for evolution in G or $\rm M_{1,2}$ over 0 < z < 1, and find that BCGs have not grown significantly (2${\times}$) faster than the cluster population for z < 1 at 3$σ$ confidence. This implies that BCGs achieve dominance and establish defining properties early (z > 1) in massive clusters. In general, we find that the Gini index is a valuable and relatively straightforward measurement, with well-controlled systematics, that could be applied to much larger samples to study BCG dominance and emergence.

title: Mid-Infrared Variability as a Probe of Hidden AGN Activity: A Comparison of Seyfert 1 and Seyfert 2 AGNs in the BAT 58-Month Sample
summary: In accordance with the AGN Unification model, the optical variability of Seyfert 2s is expected to be suppressed because the central engine is obscured by a dusty torus. The absorbed UV/optical radiation is reprocessed and re-emitted in longer wavelengths including the mid-infrared (MIR), making MIR variability a promising probe of obscured AGNs. We investigate the optical ASAS-SN and MIR NEOWISE variability of Seyfert 1 and Seyfert 2 AGNs from the \textit{Swift} 58-month BAT catalog, comparing both populations against non-variable galaxies. One of the first systematic studies of MIR AGN variability, we detected significant variability for Sy1s and the majority of Sy2s. 65% of Sy2s exhibit variability as significant as Sy1s in the MIR, especially in the W2 band, indicating torus dominated MIR variability. Additionally, 22% of Sy2s show higher variability compared to non-variable sources in the W2 band with p-value of $7.1\times 10^{-15}$. Demonstrating MIR variability as an important method to probe the variability of torus and select obscured AGN. Finally, we perform dust reverberation mapping on the Sy1 sample between the optical and W1 or W2 light curves, with measured time delays between 22-786 days (0.02-0.61 pc) for the hot dust in the inner regions of the torus. Our measured torus radius-luminosity slope, $R \propto L^{0.42\pm0.05}$, agrees with literature results. Combining the W1 and W2 band lags with archival NIR measurements, we measured the temperature profile of the torus with $T \propto R^{-α}$, where $α$ values range from 0.3-1.1.

title: Interpreting JWST UV luminosity functions and angular correlation functions via a "universal language" for high-redshift galaxies
summary: The James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) found more bright $z\gtrsim10$ galaxies than expected before its launch. No consensus has emerged on whether difficulties in reproducing them stem from missing physics, simplifying assumptions that break down at the highest redshifts, or model mis-calibration. This is complicated because most galaxy models cannot be compared like-to-like, and models invoking different physical processes can make similar predictions for compressed summaries such as ultraviolet luminosity functions (UV LFs). Here we describe galaxy populations in a universal language: a chain of physically and empirically motivated conditional distributions linking halo mass, stellar mass, star formation rate and UV magnitude, defined consistently across models and data. We build a broad prior from fits to five hydrodynamic simulations, which predict very different high-redshift galaxy populations. We infer the parameters of this flexible galaxy model from $z>6$ JWST observations of UV LFs and angular correlation functions (ACFs). Including the mass-complete ACFs disfavors a large scatter around the stellar-to-halo mass relation (SHMR). With simulation-based priors, the star-forming main sequence (SFMS) is described by a star-formation timescale of about one halo dynamical time, and the scatter around the SFMS increases toward lower stellar masses. The SFMS scatter is the main source of stochasticity in UV magnitude at fixed halo mass, accounting for a median $\sim$61% of the variance at $M_{\rm UV}=-20$ (SHMR scatter: $\sim$36%). Bayesian model selection finds no evidence for redshift evolution of the SHMR or for an SFMS slope different from unity. At $z\sim20$, our fiducial model predicts UV LFs orders of magnitude below estimates from photometric candidates. A consensus on the discrepant UV LF estimates at $z\geq14$ is needed to determine whether model extensions are required.

title: Demographic dynamics of the Japanese astronomy and astrophysics publication community during 1996-2025
summary: We investigate the demographic evolution of the Japanese astronomy and astrophysics publication community during 1996-2025 using bibliometric data from 23,274 publications in major journals in the field. The number of active Japan-affiliated authors increased from approximately 600 in the late 1990s to more than 2,000 by the early 2020s, while annual publication output reached approximately 1,400 by 2025. Participation was highly heterogeneous, with 46% of authors observed in only one publication year within the study period and a smaller core showing long observed participation periods. We define the Community Renewal Rate (CRR) as a community-level measure of renewal, calculated as the fraction of active authors not observed during a specified preceding interval. The 5-year CRR typically remained near one quarter of the active community, with annual values ranging from approximately 21% to 33%, indicating persistent renewal despite substantial community growth. An order-of-magnitude comparison suggests that newly entering students account for only part of the renewal-author population. The community therefore expanded while sustaining both continuity through authors with long observed participation periods and renewal through recurring changes in active membership.

title: Faster $χ^2$ periodogram: Accelerating linear algebra with fast Toeplitz solvers
summary: In recent years, the traditional Lomb--Scargle periodogram, relying on least-squares fitting of a sinusoid to data with a known mean, has been mostly superseded by its floating-mean extension---the generalized Lomb--Scargle periodogram---due to the superior robustness and accuracy of the latter. While further generalization to higher-degree trigonometric polynomials (known as the multiharmonic analysis of variance and the fast $χ^2$ periodogram) has been known for decades, its usage remains relatively uncommon, mostly due to its significantly higher computational cost. Here we present a technique reducing the computational complexity of such an extension by combining a Toeplitz formulation of the system of normal equations with non-uniform fast Fourier transforms, coupled with condition-number monitoring to protect against numerical instability. When modified for practical efficiency rather than asymptotic computational complexity, our approach reaches speed-ups exceeding an order of magnitude over current state-of-the-art implementations across a wide range of hyperparameters when evaluated on multithreaded systems, while matching or exceeding their accuracy. Additionally, we provide a reference implementation used for benchmarking, along with the code used to generate the results presented in this work.

title: Geometric tracking of a halo CME using full-circle wide-field views from PUNCH
summary: We tracked the large, geoeffective halo coronal mass ejection (CME) of 2025-May-31 across the very wide field of view of the Polarimeter to Unify the Corona and Heliosphere (PUNCH) mission, as a proof of concept for data-informed forecasting of CME arrival times at Earth. using simple point-and-click measurement of the front location as far as 47 degrees away from the Sun itself, we constrained an analytic "ludicrous ice-cream cone" geometric model with just three parameters: position angle, off-Earth-Sun angle, and propagation speed. We show that the model is sufficient to capture the bulk envelope of the CME, and also insufficient to capture the complexity of the CME's evolution. We generated simulated arrival-time forecasts for the CME by extrapolating the constant-velocity propagation to determine the time of impact with Earth. These "retro-forecasts" converged to within 30 +/- 15 minutes of the actual arrival time, 8 hours prior to arrival. The convergence was marked by a clear inflection point in the curve of predicted-arrival-time vs time-of-forecast. We conclude that continuous wide-field tracking is sufficiently powerful to enable even crude models to substantially improve arrival-time forecasting precision, and discuss future work required both to validate this single-event result and to extend it to more sophisticated analyses.

title: The Effect of Asphericity to the Inference of Supernova Circumstellar Environment from Radio Observations
summary: Radio observations of supernovae (SNe) enable us to constrain the circumstellar environment of their progenitor stars, and hence the mass-loss history immediately prior to the explosion. However, despite lines of evidence pointing to the aspherical configurations of circumstellar matter (CSM) around many SNe, the derivation of CSM parameters is often done under the assumption of spherically symmetric CSM. In this work, based on a recent model of radio emission from SNe interacting with aspherical CSM, we investigate how lifting the assumption of spherical symmetry affects the CSM parameter inference. First, we apply the model to mock data simulating typical observations of Type Ia-CSM, Ibc and II SNe and find that the total CSM mass required for to reproduce radio observation depends weakly on the CSM covering fraction $f_Ω$, with ${f_Ω}^{0.15-0.38}$. We then apply the model and fit the radio light curves of Type Ia-CSM SN 2020eyj. We show that, even with the assumption of asphericity as severe as $f_Ω= 0.1$, the requirement for the total CSM mass is only reduced to $\sim 50 \%$ of the value inferred in spherical models. These results demonstrate that introducing asphericity in radio emission models is often not enough to reduce the required CSM mass significantly.

title: Constraining neutrino masses with localized fast radio bursts: Current bounds and future prospects
summary: The dispersion-measure (DM)--redshift relation of fast radio bursts (FRBs) provides independent low-redshift cosmological information for neutrino-mass inference. In this work, we perform joint analyses with cosmic microwave background (CMB) data, using 120 localized FRBs with reliable host-galaxy redshifts and larger mock samples, to investigate the effects of sample size and the dark-energy model on constraints on the sum of neutrino masses, $\sum m_ν$. In the $Λ$CDM+$\sum m_ν$ model, CMB+FRB gives $\sum m_ν<0.21\,\mathrm{eV}$, substantially relaxed relative to the current CMB+DESI result. With 1000 simulated events, CMB+FRB1(mock) gives an upper limit of $0.12\,\mathrm{eV}$, which decreases to $0.035\,\mathrm{eV}$ for CMB+FRB2(mock) with 10000 events. The latter is more stringent than the CMB+DESI limit, demonstrating the potential of large localized FRB samples to constrain neutrino mass. When the model is extended to $w_0w_a$CDM+$\sum m_ν$, both the observed and mock samples yield upper limits of approximately $0.3$--$0.4\,\mathrm{eV}$, indicating that the assumed dark-energy model remains a dominant factor in these constraints. As localized FRB samples grow and the modeling of the individual DM contributions becomes more accurate, FRBs may provide further independent low-redshift information for constraining neutrino mass.

title: Global Fit Inference for LISA with samsara++
summary: The Laser Interferometer Space Antenna (LISA) will observe a superposition of gravitational-wave signals, requiring joint inference of an unknown number of sources, parameters, and instrumental noise. To disentangle these contributions, that overlap in both time and frequency, a Global Fit (GF) analysis is needed. We present samsara++, a C++/CUDA sampler designed to address this trans-dimensional GF problem. Building on the continuous-time MCMC framework of samsara, the algorithm combines birth-death processes for adding and removing sources, with mutation moves for parameter estimation. Birth and death are selected through posterior-dependent rates. Shared-memory parallelism, incremental likelihood updates, and indexed storage reduce the computational and memory costs, while parallel tempering improves the exploration of multimodal posteriors. We assess the performance using simulated one-year LISA datasets containing Galactic double white dwarf binaries and stationary Gaussian instrumental noise. Analyses of populations containing 143 and 866 binaries start from empty source models, without preliminary searches or proposals tailored to the injected population. These tests demonstrate source reconstruction and catalog generation, highlighting, at the same time, the importance of source-count, overlapping signals, and incomplete mixing on joint source and noise inference. Then we perform a separate stress test, initialized at the injected parameters, exploring a population of 16,435 binaries, corresponding to 131,480 source parameters. This run completes 15 million iterations in approximately 16 hours using about 3 GB of RAM. All together, these benchmarks show the computational feasibility of birth-death sampling for large Galactic-binary populations, and provide a foundation for extending samsara++ toward a comprehensive LISA global fit.

title: OGHReS: Discovery of a giant hub-filament system at the edge of the Galactic molecular disc
summary: We present the discovery and characterisation of G195.65$-$0.10 (also known as the $λ$-complex), a giant hub-filament system identified by the Outer Galaxy High Resolution Survey (OGHReS). The complex contains 61 spatially and kinematically coherent HiGAL clumps with a mean velocity of $V_{\rm LSR}=32.85$ km/s and a velocity dispersion between clumps of 1.97 km/s. A $Gaia$ parallax measurement of the central emission-line star MWC 137 associated with an embedded cluster gives a heliocentric distance of 5.2$^{+0.8}_{-0.6}$ kpc, placing the complex at a Galactocentric radius of 13.2 kpc. The molecular structure spans approximately $35\times63$ pc and contains $\sim 1.6\times10^{5}$ M$_\odot$ of molecular gas, including $\sim 5 \times 10^{4}$ M$_\odot$ in dense clumps. The molecular emission is organised into three prominent velocity-coherent filaments that converge on a dense central hub. Of the associated clumps, 16 are protostellar and 45 are gravitationally bound but currently starless. The protostellar clumps are significantly more concentrated towards the hub than the starless population, with median projected offsets of 6.65 and 15.83 pc, respectively. Moreover, the luminosity-to-mass ratio of the protostellar clumps decreases significantly with increasing distance from the hub, indicating that the most evolutionarily advanced sources are preferentially located in the central region. These results reveal a systematic concentration of dense gas and increasingly evolved star formation towards the hub, with organised large-scale gas motions throughout the filamentary network. The $λ$-complex therefore provides an unprecedented laboratory to understand hierarchical and high-mass star formation in the outer Galactic disc.

title: On the origin of Milky Way binary black holes with LISA
summary: Primordial black holes (PBHs) may constitute a fraction of dark matter, but distinguishing them from black holes of stellar origin remains a major challenge. We propose a new method based on the three-dimensional localization of Galactic Binary Black Holes (BBHs) by the Laser Interferometer Space Antenna (LISA). While stellar-origin BBHs are expected to be associated with the stellar distribution of the Milky Way, PBHs may trace its more extended dark matter halo. We introduce a spatial overlap ratio that compares the gravitational-wave localization of each binary with the normalized stellar and dark matter density profiles. Using a Fisher-matrix forecast and 1000 Monte Carlo realizations of a 10-year LISA mission, we find that detecting three BBHs with an overlap ratio ln B < 0 occurs in approximately 99% of simulations where BBHs trace dark matter, but in fewer than 0.1% of simulations where they follow the stellar distribution, even when including a stellar halo containing 3% of the Galactic stellar mass. These results suggest that the localization of only a few Galactic BBHs could provide strong evidence for a primordial population, offering an independent test of their possible contribution to dark matter.

title: Magnetogenesis in Low-Scale Inflation: Viability for Astrophysical Magnetic Fields
summary: The indirect evidence for magnetic fields in the intergalactic medium motivates the study of their possible primordial origin, including generation during inflation. One mechanism for inflationary magnetogenesis involves a pseudoscalar inflaton coupled to a gauge field through the interaction $g_{φγ}φF_{μν}\tilde{F}^{μν}$. In this work, we study the viability of this mechanism in the context of low scale inflation, particularly on inflationary energy scales near the electroweak (EW) scale. We find that the post inflationary amplification of the gauge fields can produce astrophysically relevant magnetic fields for $g_{φγ}\ge 360~m_{\rm pl}^{-1}$ in the absence of Schwinger backreaction for an inflationary scale around the EW scale. We then include the backreaction of the charged current generated through the Schwinger mechanism. We find that the induced current suppresses the gauge field amplification and leads to a saturation of the gauge field energy density at a value of order $m_e^4$, where $m_e$ is the electron mass. Assuming this saturation level, we find that magnetic fields above the lower bound inferred from the non detection of secondary GeV photons from blazars can be obtained when reheating occurs at temperatures below $\sim 0.3$ GeV. For an inflationary energy scale of $100~{\rm GeV}$, achieving this saturation until a reheating temperature, $T\le 0.3~{\rm GeV}$, requires a coupling strength $g_{φγ}\ge 20000~m_{\rm pl}^{-1}$. We obtain a present-day magnetic field strength of $B_0 \sim 2\times10^{-13}$ G with a coherence length of $L_{0}\sim 5\times10^{-3}$ kpc for the reheating temperature of $100$ MeV.

title: Kinetic Monte Carlo modeling of ammonium formate NH$_4^+$HCOO$^-$ and ammonium cyanate NH$_4^+$OCN$^-$ in interstellar ices
summary: JWST observations have revealed evidence for NH$_4^+$ in the ices of the Chamaeleon I dark molecular cloud, with HCOO$^-$ and OCN$^-$ likely counter ions. Laboratory experiments have demonstrated that ammonium formate and ammonium cyanate can form through acid-base reactions involving NH$_3$ at cryogenic temperatures. The formation of these two ammonium salts are simulated to investigate their formation in dark-cloud ices and assess their sensitivity to uncertainties in the chemical reaction network, including the recently considered HOCO-mediated pathway for CO$_2$ formation, as well as variations in the cosmic-ray ionization rate, cloud collapse timescale and density, and elemental depletion. Our modeling framework consists of microscopic kinetic Monte Carlo (KMC) simulations of grain-surface chemistry augmented by UCLCHEM gas-phase and physical cloud evolution simulations. The microscopic KMC method provides for explicit simulation of the location, movement and reaction of ice species, making it particularly well-suited to model acid-base chemistry of NH$_4^+$-salt formation, occurring within the ice mantle over extended timescales. The simulations produce the canonical ice-evolution sequence, with an initially H$_2$O-rich ice followed by a layer dominated by CO and CO$_2$. Salt production is dominated by NH$_4^+$HCOO$^-$, which is found to form predominantly during the H$_2$O-rich stage as its production is limited by the availability of NH$_3$. NH$_4^+$OCN$^-$ is found to form later at the interface between the H$_2$O- and CO-rich ice when the formation of its precursor acid HNCO is enabled. Despite the variations explored, the total NH$_4^+$ abundance, particularly relative to H$_2$O, remains remarkably robust and consistent with the observed abundance. Depending on the variation, a redistribution between counterions HCOO$^-$ and OCN$^-$ is observed.

title: Directionality of low-energy electron recoils in the CYGNO experiment
summary: Electron-recoil directionality can help distinguish solar-neutrino interactions from backgrounds and, together with recoil-energy measurements and three-dimensional tracking, enable neutrino-energy spectroscopy. We study the reconstruction of the initial direction of low-energy electron recoils in the CYGNO optical time-projection chamber, focusing on the 50 L LIME prototype and its high-granularity scientific CMOS (sCMOS) readout. A dedicated algorithm identifies the interaction point from the asymmetry of the track light distribution and estimates the recoil direction from the early portion of the ionization trail, before multiple scattering erases most of the directional information. The method is characterized with a detailed Monte Carlo simulation of electron recoils and detector response. Samples spanning 15 keV to 70 keV are used to optimize the algorithm parameters by minimizing the width of the reconstructed-minus-true projected-angle distribution. The projected angular response is modeled by two Gaussian components that account for its dependence on track inclination. The narrower component, associated with favorable projections approximately parallel to the Gas Electron Multiplier (GEM) plane, has a width that improves from about $20^\circ$ near 20 keV to about $12^\circ$ at 60 keV. We also quantify the fraction of events in the correctly reconstructed angular core and discuss the dominant limitations of a camera-only two-dimensional measurement.

title: Ca II IRT activity indices from $Gaia$ spectroscopy: a baseline method for photospheric contribution estimates
summary: The $Gaia$ high-resolution spectroscopic observations using Radial Velocity Spectrometer offers a unique opportunity to study stellar Ca II infrared triplet (IRT) activity. A key step in estimating activity indices is subtracting the photospheric contribution. The canonical template-based method often fails because, for many stars, the observed line cores are deeper than the model predictions, which prevents valid activity measurements. In this work, we explore an alternative approach that constructs a baseline from less active stars as a function of effective temperature (and metallicity) to represent the photospheric contribution. Our results show that, for dwarf stars, compared with the canonical method, the baseline method not only yields far more objects with valid activity measurements, but also avoids many extremely low and unreliable values (e.g., log$R'_{\rm IRT} \lesssim -6$). The Ca II IRT activity indices derived from the baseline method correlate well with other activity proxies, confirming their reliability as activity indicators. Furthermore, they show a relation with stellar rotation, not only recovering the typical rotation--activity relation, but also revealing fine structures that may be associated with different regimes in gyrochronology. Our findings suggest that the baseline method can serve as a robust alternative for deriving accurate activity estimates, and will be particularly useful for obtaining activity indices for tens of millions of stars with the upcoming $Gaia$ Data Release 4.

title: A hybrid log-likelihood-ratio statistic for single-detector SPIIR gravitational-wave searches
summary: Periods with only one detector operating accounted for 13.3 percent of the third LIGO-Virgo observing run (O3) and 29.7 percent of the first part of the fourth observing run (O4a). We present the first dedicated single-detector implementation of the Summed Parallel Infinite Impulse Response (SPIIR) pipeline for binary neutron star (BNS) and neutron star-black hole (NSBH) merger searches. Our hybrid log-likelihood ratio combines signal-consistency models for non-Gaussian glitches with a profile likelihood ratio for the signal-to-noise ratio under a Gaussian-noise model. We calibrate the glitch model by source category and trigger-rate class. We assign false alarm rates (FARs) using the measured background from the same detector and analysis chunk, extrapolating its high-ranking tail. We check the FAR assignments by comparing observed and expected cumulative background counts for BNS in O3a and NSBH in O3b at LIGO Hanford (H1) and LIGO Livingston (L1). Using O3 data and the GWTC-3 injection set, we find that, at a threshold of one false alarm per two months, the BNS sensitive distances are $136.5^{+2.9}_{-3.0}$ Mpc in L1 and $120.2^{+3.1}_{-3.3}$ Mpc in H1. These central estimates are approximately 24 and 38 percent higher, respectively, than the GWTC-3 GstLAL values of $110.5^{+3.2}_{-3.4}$ Mpc and $87.2^{+3.6}_{-3.9}$ Mpc over the same data and injection parameter ranges. GstLAL provides the only published single-detector results in GWTC-3. For NSBH, SPIIR reaches $164.1^{+6.7}_{-7.3}$ Mpc in L1 and $134.9^{+6.3}_{-7.0}$ Mpc in H1, compared with $165.1^{+6.7}_{-7.3}$ Mpc and $156.0^{+5.9}_{-6.4}$ Mpc for GWTC-3 GstLAL, respectively. Targeted searches recover triggers associated with GW190425, GW200105_162426, and GW230529_181500 with assigned FARs below the same threshold.

title: Towards the LSST DESC pipeline for cosmology with galaxy clusters -- design and validation on simulations
summary: We present the current implementation of an automated framework developed within the Legacy Survey of Space and Time Dark Energy Science Collaboration (LSST DESC) for galaxy cluster cosmology, in preparation for the first LSST data releases of the NSF-DOE Vera C. Rubin Observatory. The cluster cosmology pipeline integrates DESC-developed tools dedicated to galaxy/cluster catalog ingestion, cluster number count and weak lensing measurements, modeling, and parameter inference through posterior sampling, enabling reproducible end-to-end cluster cosmology analyses. We test and validate the pipeline using synthetic mock datasets and the LSST DESC cosmoDC2 simulation, performing a joint analysis of redMaPPer cluster abundance and stacked weak lensing profiles measured in bins of redshift and richness. We constrain two cosmological parameters, $Ω_c$ and $σ_8$, along with six cluster mass-observable relation parameters. Our baseline analysis recovers the fiducial cosmoDC2 values of $Ω_c$ and $σ_8$ within $0.51σ$ and $0.34σ$, respectively. We also showcase the flexibility of the overall pipeline by assessing the impact of fiducial cosmology and alternative modeling prescriptions on the parameter constraints. Lastly, we also discuss the current limitations of the pipeline and the developments needed for LSST data.

title: The PHAROS Spectral Library: Data Processing, Spectral Reconstruction, and Uncertainty Propagation
summary: We document the data reduction, reconstruction choices, and available uncertainty propagation underlying fifteen PHAROS stellar spectral energy distributions from 0.5 to 5000 nm. A catalogue timeline and a practical FITS guide introduce the available products, their column and extension conventions, and examples of reading, integration, and uncertainty display. Shared methods are presented once, including flux geometry, support-aware integration, X-ray likelihoods, the 2025 X/EUV luminosity relation, intrinsic Ly$α$ inference, airglow treatment, spectral junctions, and covariance-aware resampling. Target sections record the adopted observations and alternatives, including spatially separated binary components, unresolved system-level EUV measurements, direct EUVE constraints, optical stellar-twin transfer, and literature-anchored cases where new spectral inference is unsupported. The distinction between native measurement errors, conditional model intervals, empirical predictive scatter, and physical-method sensitivity is maintained. Signed measurements and nonnegative irradiation products are distinguished. Each target section concludes with the final nominal spectrum and its available uncertainty bounds on common axes. This library provides the detailed provenance and interpretation needed to accompany the catalogue paper and its machine-readable products.

title: Independent interferometric observable confirms black hole shadow in M87*
summary: A new epoch for direct visualisation of accretion dynamics near a black hole's event horizon began when the Event Horizon Telescope Collaboration (EHTC) synthesised an Earth-sized aperture with millimeter radio interferometry and published the first reconstructed image of a black hole shadow at the core of radio galaxy Messier 87 (M87). The image appeared as a ring-like structure, representing the gravitationally lensed and redshifted emission around the central supermassive black hole, M87*, located at the galactic nucleus. However, application of various data analysis and imaging heuristics resulted in divergent representations of M87* fine-scale features, with some external analyses even challenging the fundamental ring-like morphology of the source. Such difficulties arise as a consequence of the inherent sparsity of the very-long baseline interferometry (VLBI) measurements, rendering interferometric image reconstruction an inadequately constrained problem. Moreover, the solution is sensitive to instrument calibration, post-processing algorithms, and imaging hyperparameters. Here, we apply a newly-developed independent imaging algorithm to the M87* dataset, which is free from prescriptive morphological priors and founded on observables immune to instrument calibration errors. We reconstruct the black hole shadow image, and unequivocally reproduce a ring-like morphology, with angular diameter 42.2 +/- 1.5 microarcseconds corresponding to a black hole mass of 6.5 +/- 0.5 billion solar masses assuming nominal scaling parameters, observed at an inclination angle of ~20 deg from the approaching jet.

title: Tracing the Luminosity Evolution of Globular Cluster Systems with JWST: MACS J1149.5+2223 at z=0.544
summary: We present a study of the compact-source population associated with the massive galaxy cluster MACS J1149.5+2223 at z=0.544 using deep JWST/NIRCam imaging in F115W, F150W, and F200W. After photometric and morphological selection, we identify 1,202 unresolved compact-source candidates. The observed luminosity distribution samples only the bright side of the expected globular-cluster luminosity function (GCLF), remaining several magnitudes above the turnover. Based on published GCLF turnovers for Abell 2744 and MACS 0417, we adopt an expected turnover magnitude of m_0=33.66 mag for MACS 1149. A forward-modeled fit then yields sigma=1.71 mag, which characterizes the observed bright-side slope under the adopted turnover rather than the intrinsic width of the full GCLF. Comparison with PARSEC simple stellar population models shows that the elevated luminosities of the compact sources are consistent with the expected fading of younger stellar populations as they evolve toward the present epoch. The brightest sources reach luminosities comparable to those of ultra-compact dwarfs. However, stellar-population degeneracies and possible foreground contamination make it difficult to distinguish. Together with recent JWST studies of globular cluster systems across a range of redshifts, MACS 1149 extends the emerging observational sequence of compact stellar systems and supports stellar population fading as an important contributor to their luminosity evolution across cosmic time.

title: Advancing Electroformed X-ray Optics Bridging Synchrotron Radiation Technology and Space Astronomy: Improved Figure Accuracy and X-ray Imaging Performancev
summary: We have developed high-resolution electroformed nickel X-ray telescope mirrors by extending precision mirror-fabrication techniques developed for synchrotron X-ray microscopy to space astronomy. Our previous study identified axial figure errors of a replicated mirror as one of the factors limiting its X-ray angular resolution. In the present study, we fabricated a new mirror using a substantially improved mandrel and directly compared the two-dimensional figure errors of the mandrels and replicated inner mirror surfaces for both the previous and new mandrel--mirror pairs. This comparison reveals how contributions to the final mirror figure errors changed with improved mandrel accuracy. For the previous mirror, the mandrel and mirror showed a strong spatial correlation in their figure errors, indicating that a substantial component of the mirror figure pattern was inherited from the mandrel. In contrast, after improving the mandrel figure, the new mirror exhibited a weaker mandrel--mirror spatial correlation, while the residual figure deviations arising between the mandrel and final mirror became comparable in magnitude to the residual mandrel figure errors. The improved mandrel reduced the central 68% widths, W68, of the axial slope error distribution from 3.3 to 1.6 arcsec for the paraboloidal surface and from 5.0 to 1.1 arcsec for the hyperboloidal surface. Correspondingly, the mirror values improved from 4.6 to 2.4 arcsec and from 12.4 to 2.0 arcsec, respectively. X-ray measurements at 12 keV yielded local half power diameters (HPDs) of approximately 7--17 arcsec and a full-aperture HPD of 8.5 arcsec. The newly fabricated mirror was adopted for the soft X-ray telescope of the fifth Focusing Optics X-ray Solar Imager (FOXSI-5) sounding rocket flight and was successfully flown in May 2026.

title: Neural Surrogates for Tabulated Nuclear Equations of State in Core-Collapse Supernova Simulations
summary: Large-scale core-collapse supernova simulations rely on tabulated nuclear equations of state (EOSs), whose memory requirements can become a practical constraint in massively parallel calculations. We explore a compact alternative by replacing the tabulated thermodynamic mapping with a neural-network surrogate, using the Lattimer--Swesty EOS as a representative reference model. The surrogate directly predicts pressure, sound speed, and effective adiabatic index from $(\log ρ, \log e, Y_e)$ and accurately reconstructs the nonlinear thermodynamic structure of the EOS, including its behavior across phase-transition regions. It reproduces one-dimensional shock-tube solutions with hydrodynamic errors at the $\sim 10^{-3}$ level under different thermodynamic conditions and yields hydrostatic equilibrium configurations closely matching those obtained with the reference EOS. We find that smaller regression errors do not necessarily yield better hydrodynamic performance, demonstrating the importance of hydrodynamic validation in surrogate model selection. A compact network with only $\sim 10^4$ parameters retains this accuracy while reducing the memory required to store the EOS from $\sim 160$ MB to $\sim 100$ KB, corresponding to a reduction by a factor of $\sim 1500$. The surrogate also remains stable through collapse, bounce, shock formation, and post-bounce evolution in a one-dimensional adiabatic core-collapse calculation. These results demonstrate the potential of compact neural EOS surrogates for reducing memory requirements in large-scale core-collapse supernova simulations.

title: Baryon Acoustic Oscillations from the all-sky Wen & Han cluster catalog and the 2MASS Redshift Survey
summary: Baryon acoustic oscillations (BAO) in the clustering of galaxies and quasars now measure distances to precision of about one percent although galaxy clusters have so far given only marginal signals. We measure the BAO scale in the correlation function of \vNclus\ galaxy clusters with spectroscopic redshifts at $0.1<z<0.7$ from the Wen and Han (2024) all-sky catalog. After reconstruction of the density field, the BAO peak has a significance of $\vsigpostσ$ against a model without it, and gives $\DV/\rd=\vDVpost\pm\vDVpoststat\,({\rm stat})\pm\vDVpostsys\,({\rm sys})$ at an effective redshift $z_{\rm eff}=\vzeffv$, a \vfracposttot\% distance. We find that the statistical uncertainty is \vratiostat\ times smaller than that of the best earlier cluster measurement. The distance agrees with the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI) Data Release 2 within $\vnsdesipostσ$ and lies $\vnsplanckpostσ$ below Planck. We also measure the BAO scale in the \vTNgal\ galaxies of the 2MASS Redshift Survey with a mean effective redshift (weighted by $n\,w^2$ with FKP weights), $z_{\rm eff}=\vTzeff$ For this all-sky galaxy sample we obtain $\aiso=\vTpreA^{+\vTpreAup}_{-\vTpreAlo}$ before reconstruction.

title: Initial Conditions Dictate Gas-Stellar Counter-Rotation in Galaxies
summary: We present a physical origin of gas-stellar counter-rotation in galaxies. Scale-dependent partitions of tidal torques from cosmic primordial perturbations source angular momentum for distinct baryonic components. This scale dependence maps to radial hierarchy in Lagrangian space clustering: stellar components, assembled at earlier times from the inner protohalo, retain persistent memory of small-scale tidal torques, whereas gas, accreted later from outer Lagrangian regions, is governed by large-scale perturbations and can develop counter-rotation. This mechanism is observationally testable and offers a direct probe of the hierarchical cold dark matter (CDM) paradigm. Unlike conventional late-time scenarios that only explain the existence of counter-rotation, our framework further predicts its component-resolved direction, enabling component-resolved angular momentum to serve as a new probe of primordial density perturbations and improving cosmological initial condition reconstruction.

title: OGLE-2018-BLG-0829L: A Microlensing System with a Planet Orbiting a Star Possessing a Brown-Dwarf Companion
summary: We analyze the microlensing event OGLE-2018-BLG-0829, whose light curve exhibits a weak short-term anomaly in addition to the prominent caustic-crossing features of a binary lens. The anomaly cannot be explained by a binary-lens single-source (2L1S) model. We therefore investigate both binary-lens binary-source (2L2S) and triple-lens single-source (3L1S) interpretations and find that both models reproduce the additional anomaly, with the 3L1S model being favored by $Δχ^2=15.1$. Under the favored 3L1S interpretation, the anomaly arises from a caustic induced by a planetary-mass companion, whereas the prominent caustic-crossing features are produced by the underlying binary lens. Combining the measured event timescale, $t_{\rm E}=7.55\pm0.30$ days, and angular Einstein radius, $θ_{\rm E}=0.325 \pm 0.059$ mas, with a Bayesian analysis, we infer a lens system consisting of an M dwarf of mass $0.193^{+0.300}_{-0.098}\,M_\odot$, a possible brown-dwarf companion of mass $0.068^{+0.105}_{-0.034}\,M_\odot$, and a Saturn-mass planet of mass $0.337^{+0.522}_{-0.171}\,M_{\rm J}$. The companions have projected separations of approximately 3.6 au and 1.6 au from the primary, respectively. However, the physical interpretation remains tentative because potentially important higher-order effects have not been considered, and the dynamical stability of the proposed configuration remains uncertain. If confirmed, this would be the third star--brown dwarf--planet system identified through microlensing, highlighting the potential of microlensing to detect planets in complex multiple systems.

title: Comets in Kepler background photometry: the ion tail and tail disconnection of C/2009 K5 (McNaught) and an analysis of comets crossing the Kepler field
summary: Kepler recorded several thousand dedicated sky-background pixels per detector output every 29.4 min from 2009 to 2013, an archive that we use to study comets. During 2010 April 14-21 a narrow band of excess light swept across the field at 1.46 deg/day. This feature is the ion tail of comet C/2009 K5 (McNaught), whose head passed just beyond the edge of the detector array. We trace the tail from 0.9 deg to ~13 deg from the nucleus at surface brightnesses of 26.7-30 mag/arcsec^2; its aberration implies a solar-wind speed of ~500-750 km/s. At 30-min cadence we follow a tail-disconnection event on 2010 April 17-19 whose timing and geometry are consistent with a flank encounter with a coronal mass ejection, although other triggers cannot be excluded. We then analyze all 21 known comets with perihelion distance q < 15 AU whose heads crossed the detectors, using photometry at the predicted head positions calibrated against displaced control tracks. Eight comets are detected, including C/2010 J4 (WISE) a few days before its discovery and two comets at 6.3-7.4 AU with one-sided streaks that we interpret as dust tails. The undetected comets give 3-sigma limits of typically Kp > 16.6-18.1 within 5 arcmin of the head. A blind shift-and-stack search for moving diffuse sources, roughly 50% complete at Kp ~ 15.5-16 for rates of 0.3-1 deg/day, recovers four known comets and finds no unknown ones. Animations show the K5 tail and comets C/2011 L3 and C/2010 J4 crossing the field.

title: Validation of Ariel candidates orbiting K-M stars
summary: One of the key goals of planetary population studies is to achieve broad coverage of the parameter space, which is not yet fully represented by confirmed planets. This limitation can be mitigated by including planets that have been statistically validated through a vetting procedure, even if they are not fully confirmed. In preparation for the Ariel mission, a Mission Candidate Sample has been assembled, comprising both confirmed planets and several unvalidated candidates. In this context, we apply a vetting analysis to a selected subsample of these candidates. Our methodology is based on the TRICERATOPS tool, aimed at confirming the presence of transiting planets or ruling out false-positive scenarios. We applied TRICERATOPS to a sample of 318 targets drawn from the last three Ariel TESS Planet Candidates catalogues. The analysis includes evaluation of statistical probabilities, as well as checks on stellar binarity indicators such as the Renormalized Unit Weight Error (RUWE) and the IPD_frac_multi_peak values from Gaia Data Release 3. Our analysis validated 56 candidates as planets, identified 29 false positives, and classified 35 as likely planets. These results are intended to support the Ariel mission by providing a probabilistic priority ranking to guide follow-up observations and optimise targets for atmospheric characterisation studies.

title: A COMPASS to the Galaxy: Joint nucleosynthetic yield set comparison and parameter inference in Galactic chemical evolution
summary: Galactic Chemical Evolution (GCE) models connect stellar nucleosynthesis to observed abundance patterns, but their interpretation requires simultaneous parameter inference and comparison between competing stellar yield prescriptions. This remains challenging due to intractable likelihoods and growing dataset complexity. Using compass, a novel simulation-based inference framework, we perform, for the first time, amortized joint Bayesian model comparison and parameter inference for GCE models with intractable likelihoods within a unified architecture. Compass employs a conditional score-based diffusion model with a transformer architecture to learn both the posterior and likelihood directly from forward simulations, enabling efficient inference and likelihood-based ranking of competing nucleosynthetic yield sets. In controlled tests, compass identifies the generating yield set and recovers ground-truth parameters with accuracy comparable to existing simulation-based inference (SBI) methods, while reducing computational cost by orders of magnitude. Applied to Milky Way data, the framework favors a hybrid NuGrid + IllustrisTNG yield prescription, confirmed by an independent classifier, and infers an initial mass function slope of $α_{\rm IMF} = -2.65 \pm 0.02$ and a SN$_{\rm Ia}$ normalization of $\log(N_{\rm Ia}) = -2.81 \pm 0.02$, with a systematic spread of $\approx 0.3$ in $α_{\rm IMF}$ between the best-ranked yield sets, consistent with independent constraints. The attention mechanism confirms that the inferred parameters are driven by physically meaningful abundance signatures. By unifying amortized parameter inference, Bayesian model comparison, and interpretability in a single probabilistic framework, compass provides a scalable approach for precision chemical evolution studies with current and forthcoming spectroscopic surveys.

title: Mapping the obscured Galactic disk: ERIS J-band low-resolution spectroscopy of 27 Classical Cepheids
summary: Classical Cepheids (CCs) are standard candles and key tracers of young stellar populations. However, their use in the most obscured regions is hampered by the high interstellar extinction at optical wavelengths. Near-infrared spectroscopy offers major advantages by greatly reducing absorption corrections and enabling access to regions of the Milky Way that are still poorly sampled. In this work, we determine the atmospheric parameters and abundances of Fe, Mg and Si for a sample of 27 CCs based on observations with ERIS@VLT in J-band low-resolution mode ($R \sim 4000$). Combining PySME with 1D MARCS atmosphere models and non local thermal equilibrium grids, we simultaneous optimise the atmospheric parameters through spectral fitting. This method is validated with a direct comparison with high-resolution optical investigations and re-analysis of archive optical spectra for the targets in common. The results show good consistency in both metallicity and chemical abundances. We obtain mean abundance ratios of $\mathrm{\langle[Mg/Fe]\rangle=0.01\pm0.12~dex}$ and $\mathrm{\langle[Si/Fe]\rangle=0.10\pm0.09~dex}$, in agreement with reference samples. Moreover, we provide for the first time the Mg and Si abundances of 12 CCs. Finally, we have found distinct kinematic properties for two of the most distant Galactic CCs, located at Galactocentric distances of $\mathrm{\approx 28-29~kpc}$ and with extreme values of vertical height, $\mathrm{\approx +4.8~kpc}$ and $\mathrm{\approx -5.3~kpc}$; more data are required to constrain their nature. Our results confirm that J-band spectroscopy at low-resolution can be used as a good diagnostic for the chemical investigation in highly obscured Galactic regions, otherwise inaccessible at optical wavelengths.

title: Gravitational Potential of CALIFA Galaxies from the Blue Cloud to the Red Sequence
summary: We explore the gravitational potential of 238 (E1$-$Sdm) CALIFA galaxies from the Blue cloud to the Red Sequence using the star formation rate$-$stellar mass diagram ($\mathrm{SFR}-M_\star$) diagnosis. On average, galaxies in the Blue cloud possess slow-rising circular velocity curves (CVCs), those in the Green valley have flat CVCs, while galaxies in the Red sequence are characterised with peaked CVCs. Both the maximum circular velocity ($V_{c,\mathrm{max}}$) and asymptotic circular velocity ($V_{c,\mathrm{flat}}$) of the galaxies increase from the Blue cloud to the Red sequence, and show approximately linear relations with the logarithmic offsets from the star-forming main sequence ($Δ\mathrm{SFR}$s). The $Δ\mathrm{SFR}-\log_{10}(V_{c,\mathrm{max}})$ relation has a steeper slope ($-0.154 \pm 0.012$) than the $Δ\mathrm{SFR}-\log_{10}(V_{c,\mathrm{flat}})$ relation ($-0.124 \pm 0.011$). These results suggest that $V_{c,\mathrm{max}}$, tracing the inner gravitational potential, indicates a stronger variation along the quenching parameter $Δ\mathrm{SFR}$ than $V_{c,\mathrm{flat}}$, which is more strongly influenced by the outer mass distribution and dark matter halo.

title: Compositions of Exoplanetary Debris Shaped by Milky Way Stellar Abundance Patterns
summary: Galactic chemical evolution (GCE) predicts large-scale variations in exoplanet compositions with host star elemental abundances, reflecting the Milky Way's history of star formation and elemental enrichment from stellar feedback. We investigate the impact of GCE on the compositions of exoplanetary bodies using polluted white dwarfs (WDs), which probe the bulk elemental abundances of planetary debris. Using a literature sample of 70 polluted WDs, we calculate iron mass fractions for the accreted bodies and compare these to tracers of the WD progenitor's initial abundances, including age and kinematics. We demonstrate predicted trends using a sample of main sequence stars, and we show that these are generally reflected in the polluted WD sample. In particular, H-dominated WDs show preferentially larger iron mass fractions amongst younger and less dynamically excited systems. This trend is weaker amongst He-dominated WDs, and we show that this may be attributed to uncertainties in their observed phases of accretion. Continuing to combine WD pollution compositions with stellar parameters and kinematics could be a valuable way to constrain large-scale versus local drivers of planetary compositions.

title: Unexpected Plateau: The Constant $ \rm \log ε(Th/Eu)$ Ratio of Actinide-Boost Stars
summary: The astrophysical site of the rapid neutron-capture process ($r$-process) is still one of the major open questions in astronomy. A key mystery is the origin of the peculiar actinide-to-lanthanide ratio found in the so called actinide-boost stars, with $ \rm \log ε(Th/Eu)>-0.35$. Here we present the largest sample of Th measurements in stars formed in an external galaxy, Gaia Sausage Enceladus. From this sample, we present the three most metal-rich actinide-boost stars discovered to date, $\rm -1.6<[Fe/H]<-1.1$. In addition, we measured Th in a comparison sample of Milky Way stars formed in situ, and compiled Th measurements from the literature which do not account for non-local thermodynamic equilibrium (NLTE) effects. After applying NLTE corrections to the combined sample, a bimodality in the $\rm\logε(Th/Eu)$ ratio is revealed. Unexpectedly, actinide-boost stars lie on a very narrow $(σ=0.02)$ plateau of $\rm \logε(Th/Eu)=-0.2$, clearly separated from actinide-normal stars. Most (if not all) of the actinide-boost stars in our sample originate from outside the Milky Way. Chemical evolution models show that such a plateau can arise, even at [Fe/H] = $-$1, when a single actinide-rich event dominates the r-process content of a small or gas-depleted system. Combined with other evidence, our results suggest that mergers with neutron stars are the most promising astrophysical site for actinide-boost stars.

title: Probing superradiant cloud level transitions in stellar-mass black hole binaries with milli-Hertz and multiband gravitational wave observations
summary: We investigate superradiant cloud level transitions in stellar-mass black hole binaries with milli-Hertz and multiband gravitational-wave observations. Under the adopted cloud formation and survival conditions, the $\lvert322\rangle\rightarrow\lvert31-1\rangle$ fine transition can imprint phase corrections in the LISA band, while Bohr transitions occurring after the milli-Hertz band observation can be probed through shifts in the merger time. Modeling the coupled cloud-orbit evolution, we find that cloud depletion can begin before resonance and that ionization can advance rather than delay coalescence. For a representative nearby binary, a vacuum injection-recovery analysis yields a cloud-mass-fraction posterior concentrated at $M_c^i/M\lesssim10^{-6}$. Comparing the LISA-predicted coalescence time with a subsequent ground-based measurement provides a complementary test of later cloud evolution. These results motivate complementary searches for ultralight bosons with milli-Hertz and multiband gravitational-wave observations.
